title: Wendell and the Ledger
premise: When estate lawyer August Vane is summoned to read the will of reclusive matriarch Edith Calloway, he discovers a document dated three days after her confirmed death—and a body in the conservatory dressed entirely in clothes from his own wardrobe. As Detective Imogen Reyes investigates, August realizes the killer is using his own meticulous case files to stage the murders, implicating him in crimes he only documented. The will's true beneficiary list matches exactly seven people whose secrets August buried over seven years of quiet legal work. To clear his name and stop the killings, August must weaponize his own archive against an adversary who learned filing from watching him—ultimately revealing that the 'dead' Edith faked her death to expose the town's corruption, and that her loyal groundskeeper Wendell has been executing her ledger of debts. In the final confrontation, August chooses truth over loyalty, publishing the ledger and surrendering his own complicity.
about_author: Gideon Dunmore is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade handling probate files in coastal New England before turning to fiction. His debut draws on years of watching how paper can outlive, and outmaneuver, the people it describes.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: August Vane's POV. Called to Calloway House at dawn, August reads a will postdated beyond Edith Calloway's death certificate, his hands steady out of professional habit while dread builds beneath. The emotional beat is controlled unease—the first crack in seven years of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: August's POV. The groundskeeper Wendell finds a stranger dead in the conservatory, wearing August's own missing gray suit. Detective Imogen Reyes arrives and notes the fit is too perfect to be coincidence. The beat is vertigo: August's private world made public evidence against him.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: August's POV, with a flashback thread. He audits his own case files and realizes each of the seven beneficiaries named in the false will corresponds to a secret he once filed away for powerful clients. The beat is dawning horror: someone has read his archive like scripture.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Doesn't Blink
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. She interviews August, catching the micro-tells of a man who knows more than he says, while quietly confirming the dead man had no identity at all—a ghost assembled from records. The beat is cat-and-mouse tension between two people who both trust documents over people.

chapters.title: The Second Entry
chapters.summary: August's POV. Beneficiary number two dies staged inside another client's sealed estate, and a page torn from August's own file is left on the body like a signature. The beat is accelerating panic as August understands the killer is working down his ledger in order.

chapters.title: What Wendell Saw
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, intimate and oblique. The old groundskeeper tends the graves, quotes Edith's sayings, and watches August dig through the greenhouse where she spent her last year. The beat is quiet menace—loyalty so absolute it reads as devotion or threat, impossible to tell apart.

chapters.title: The Archive Turns
chapters.summary: August's POV. He tries to destroy the incriminating files but finds key pages already replaced with forgeries so precise they could only be his own hand imitated. Reyes confronts him with the discrepancies. The beat is betrayal by one's own methods; the trap closes.

chapters.title: Edith's Last Instruction
chapters.summary: August's POV, racing pace. Following a codicil hidden in a probate precedent he filed himself, August discovers Edith alive in a care cottage, having staged her death to force the town's hidden debts into the open. The beat is revelation reframing everything: the will was bait, and August was chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: The Ledger Settled
chapters.summary: Alternating August and Wendell POV. Wendell, revealed as Edith's executor of reckoning, corners August among the gravestones; Edith arrives to stop the final killing, but not before Wendell forces August to choose between burning the ledger and publishing it. The beat is the climax: loyalty versus truth made physical.

chapters.title: Filed Under V
chapters.summary: August's POV, weeks later. The ledger goes public, the corrupt beneficiaries face consequences, Wendell surrenders without resistance, and Edith vanishes again—leaving August one final document: his own confession, signed. The beat is bittersweet resolution: visibility chosen at last, at the cost of the invisible life he built.
